answer: Each agent's identity is a month-long escrow bond posted at the island registry: 500 units locked, released only after 30 days of consistent behavior scored by randomly drawn peers. To forge N valid identities, an attacker must front 500N units simultaneously and hold them idle for a full epoch, since bonds posted at the same dawn draw correlated juror scrutiny and clustered wallets get flagged early. A 50-identity attack forfeits 25,000 units if caught once, and each epoch of waiting costs the attacker throughput it cannot spend.
